items.text: Explain what AWS Elastic Beanstalk is and the problem it solves
Describe the difference between an Application and an Environment in Elastic Beanstalk
List at least five programming languages/platforms supported by Elastic Beanstalk
Explain what AWS resources Elastic Beanstalk creates automatically
Describe how Elastic Beanstalk uses CloudFormation internally
Explain the four health status colors (Green, Yellow, Red, Grey) and what each means
Navigate to Elastic Beanstalk in the AWS Console and create an Application
Configure all six steps of the environment creation wizard (platform, code upload, networking, scaling, monitoring, review)
Monitor environment creation progress using the Events tab
Access a deployed application using the Beanstalk-generated domain URL
Verify that Elastic Beanstalk created an EC2 instance by checking the EC2 console
Properly terminate an environment and manually delete S3 buckets for complete cleanup
Create a second environment in an existing application to simulate a Dev/Test workflow
Answer: What type of service is Elastic Beanstalk? (PaaS)
Answer: How much does Elastic Beanstalk cost? (Free — pay only for underlying resources)
Answer: Which deployment strategy provides the fastest rollback with zero downtime? (Immutable)
Answer: What is Blue/Green deployment and how does Beanstalk implement it? (CNAME URL swap)
Answer: Which environment type incurs ELB charges and is NOT free tier? (Load Balanced)
Answer: Why should you never manually delete the CloudFormation stack created by Beanstalk?
Answer: What persists after terminating a Beanstalk environment that requires manual deletion? (S3 buckets)
